subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Follow-up after shunt surgery for hydrocephalus
subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm 86 years old, and I'm a male. I'm here for a follow-up after my shunt surgery for hydrocephalus. I've been doing better, but I wanted to check in and see how I'm doing. Doctor: Thank you for providing that information. Could you please tell me more about your symptoms since the surgery? Have you experienced any new or worsening symptoms, such as headaches, dizziness, or changes in your balance? Patient: No, I haven't had any headaches or dizziness since the surgery. My balance has improved a bit—I can walk to the dining room now without help, though I still need my daughter sometimes. I don't feel like I'm getting worse, but I'm not sure if I'm as good as I could be. Doctor: Have you experienced any changes in your cognitive function, such as memory issues or confusion, since your shunt surgery? Additionally, have you had any recent falls or difficulty with activities of daily living? Patient: I think my thinking is better than before. I don't feel lost when I talk to someone anymore. My daughter says I can have a normal conversation with her again, which is nice to hear. I haven't had any falls recently, and I can manage most of my daily activities with some help, but nothing serious. Doctor: Have you undergone any cognitive or neurological assessments since the shunt surgery? If so, what were the results? Patient: I was told I had a memory test where I scored 26 out of 30 on spelling and 25 out of 30 on calculations, which was an improvement from before the surgery. I wasn't able to remember any words without help before, but now I can with some prompting. Doctor: Could you please provide the results of the most recent neurological examination, including any findings related to motor function, coordination, and cognitive assessment? Patient: I was told that my gait score was between six to eight out of 12 and my balance score was 12 out of 16, for a total of 18 to 20
